content.title: About
content.content: Diet root beer is a non‑alcoholic carbonated beverage with the characteristic flavor of sassafras root, vanilla, anise and spices. The diet version uses artificial sweeteners instead of sugar, making it low‑calorie.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Root beer originated in North America in the 19th century as a homemade herbal brew.
Traditional flavor is achieved with sassafras root extract, though many modern brands use flavorings.
Diet versions appeared in the 1970s alongside the rise of low‑calorie products.
In the US, root beer is often served over ice in a “flat glass” and sometimes with a scoop of vanilla ice cream (root beer float).
Some brands sweeten their diet root beer with stevia or sucralose.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Diet root beer contains 0–5 kcal per 100 ml, allowing enjoyment without a significant energy load.

items.title: Sugar‑free
items.content: The absence of sugar makes it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose levels.

items.title: Contains plant extracts
items.content: Sassafras and anise extracts may provide mild antioxidant effects.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any carbonated drink, it contributes to fluid intake when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Alcohol‑free
items.content: Appropriate for all ages, including children and pregnant women, provided there are no contraindications to artificial sweeteners.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to sucralose, aspartame or other sweeteners, experiencing gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Excessive consumption of carbonated drinks can cause bloating and discomfort in people with irritable bowel syndrome.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic pH may contribute to tooth enamel erosion with frequent use.

items.title: Allergy to flavorings
items.content: Rarely, allergic reactions to plant extracts such as sassafras can occur.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve chilled, optionally over ice. Commonly used as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails or in a root beer float with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 7–10 days.
